risks.note: Delays arising from design changes, site conditions, labour shortages, material availability or customer approvals may impact project schedules, costs and profitability. This is not theoretical for GCC: the Chairman reports that FY26 opened with prolonged and heavier monsoon conditions disrupting execution timelines across project sites in the first half, with the year only rescued by stronger execution momentum in H2.

A significant portion of revenue is generated from a limited number of customers and industries; any slowdown in customer capex or loss of key clients could affect business performance. The order book is anchored on a handful of large industrial groups — UltraTech, Adani Power, JSW and JK Lakshmi Cement — with a single Adani Group power project (2x800 MW BoP in Madhya Pradesh) and a further Rs 260 Crores Adani order forming a large part of the power segment.

Cement plant construction remains 76.06% of the order book and 83.93% of FY26 revenue even after the Company's stated diversification (cement's order-book share has fallen from 96% to 76%). GCC's revenue therefore tracks the cement industry's capacity-addition cycle, and the diversification into power, steel, logistics parks and process industries is still at an early stage.

Growth depends on the ability to continuously secure new orders in a competitive bidding environment; reduced order inflows would impact future revenue visibility. The FY26 order book is a step-change (₹1,291 Crores versus ₹438 Crores) built on inflows of over ₹1,500 Crores in a single year, so the base for repeating that inflow is now much higher.

Fluctuations in the prices of steel, cement, fuel and other construction inputs may impact project costs and margins, particularly for fixed-price contracts. Mitigation relies on contractual price escalation clauses 'wherever feasible', strategic procurement planning and vendor diversification — leaving residual exposure on contracts without escalation protection, which matters at a 10.15% EBITDA margin.
risks.risk: Raw material and cost escalation risk

risks.note: EPC projects require significant working capital, and delays in customer certifications or collections can affect cash flows and liquidity. FY26 already shows the strain of scaling: trade receivables rose to ₹7,034.00 lakhs from ₹2,776.79 lakhs, the trade receivables turnover ratio fell 42%, the net capital turnover ratio fell 53% and the inventory turnover ratio fell 29% on inventory accumulated for newly awarded projects.

The construction industry remains labour-intensive; shortages of skilled manpower or disruptions in labour availability may affect project execution. GCC depends on a project workforce of 8,000+ personnel mobilised through an established network of site contractors, on top of its 1,400+ permanent employees.

Breakdowns or inadequate availability of construction equipment may delay project execution and reduce productivity. GCC's asset-backed model — 270+ owned machines and continuing IPO-funded equipment purchases — is both the mitigation and the source of the exposure, since utilisation of that fleet underpins the cost advantage it claims over third-party hire.
